extracted.intended_audience: school principals, proposal writers, and local school staff preparing Title III (ESEA) grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and a step-by-step procedure for developing a Title III (ESEA) preliminary and formal proposal at the elementary-school/district level, including needs assessment, committee planning, required forms, budget, staffing, and submission checkpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Four process components (subject, writer, elements, strategies)
rubrics_metrics.description: The four process components were identified to be: the subject, the writer, the elements of the proposal, and the strategies for execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four components as the organizing framework for proposal development: decide the substantive subject (topic), designate the proposal writer, enumerate required proposal elements (forms, budget, abstract, assurances, staff lists, dissemination, etc.), and plan strategies to execute and obtain approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs assessment and ranking of needs
rubrics_metrics.description: School needs were ranked and identified through a historical background, current school needs assessment, reading test data, teacher and parent input, and alignment with state Action Goals for the Seventies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct a documented needs assessment (test scores, teacher/parent discussions, local context) and rank needs to determine focus; evidence of severity and local critical need strengthens justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involve community members and school staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedure was designed to involve community members and the school staff in the appraisal of funding opportunities, the development of topics and objectives, the establishment of timetable and work deadlines, and checkpoints in the approval process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form planning committees including PTA officers, assistant principals, specialists, and parents; hold planning sessions to pool effort, secure teacher/parent input, and gain proposal support—document participants and meeting notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objective clarity (project objectives and measurable targets)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project objectives should be explicit; example objective: increase reading by a median gain of ten months for participating pupils.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State measurable, time-bound objectives (e.g., median gain target), tie objectives to activities, and specify how outcomes will be measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable and strict deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal work had very strict time limits. The four key dates were: workshop date, proposals due to Government Funding Office/Board of Education, Board of Education deadline, and OSPI closing date for submission. Efficiency of effort was a necessary prerequisite; any delays in approvals could result in missing the deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a detailed timetable with check dates and committee meetings; missing deadlines can disqualify your application—plan backward from submission dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Checkpoints in the approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Four checkpoints in the approval process were used: District Superintendent review, Area Associate Superintendent, editorial staff of Government Funded Programs/Board review, and Board of Education approval prior to submission to OSPI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anticipate multiple internal approvals; prepare to revise per reviewers' suggestions at each checkpoint and allow time for rework before final deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of proposal success (approval, participation, response, academic growth)
rubrics_metrics.description: The process was evaluated as effective on the basis of approval of the proposal, involvement of parents and staff, response to identified school needs, and academic growth consistent with the effort expended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these four success metrics when designing and later assessing the project: (1) approvals obtained; (2) parent and staff participation levels; (3) alignment with identified needs; (4) measurable academic gains relative to effort.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal format and required documents (letters, assurances, forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Required elements included LETTER OF INTENT, LETTER OF TRANSMITTAL, ASSURANCES FOR INITIAL APPLICATION, FORM A14 (statistical data), abstract, detailed budget (equipment list), and project narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the exact format provided by the funding authority; include all specified forms and attachments (legal authority docs, assurances, signatures, notarization) and do not omit required sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances and legal compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant must give assurances: necessary legal authority to apply, administration under supervision of applicant, participation of persons broadly representative of the area, funds will not supplant local funds, compliance with Title VI and HEW regulations, and other required policies and reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach substantiating legal documents, completed assurances forms (HEW 441 where applicable), and ensure non-discrimination and compliance language is present and signed by authorized representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting and equipment itemization
rubrics_metrics.description: Items of equipment costing $50.00 or more each must be itemized; a detailed equipment list and grand total must be provided (example total $7,450; grand total $56,100).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a line-item budget with quantities, descriptions, unit and total costs; justify major purchases and ensure consistency with project activities. Show total funds requested and funding period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract and project summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The abstract should briefly state project objectives, procedures, number of pupils served, expected measurable outcomes, amount requested, and a concise description of methods (e.g., videotape-based reading enrichment with 20 field trips followed by instruction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep abstract concise (one page), state who will be served, major activities, measurable goals, and summary of expected gains; this is often used in initial screening.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target population and area served
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define area served (Van Vlissingen School and neighboring schools), target population characteristics (numbers, minority status, socioeconomic context), and how program addresses state-identified critical needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include demographic/statistical information, percent handicapped if relevant, and demonstrate how the local need dovetails with state priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology and instructional design
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe specific activities and instructional methods (e.g., videotape recording of field trips, scripts, 20 field trips, each followed by six instruction periods, development of miniunits, teacher schedules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed implementation plans, schedules, lesson/unit descriptions, staff responsibilities, and how classroom teachers will integrate project activities into instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing plan and role definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: List staff funded by the grant (project teacher, teacher aides, video technician, secretary) and staff not funded (classroom teachers), with specific duties for each role (e.g., project teacher schedules trips, develops miniunits, provides inservice).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate grant-funded roles vs existing staff responsibilities; include job descriptions, time allocations, qualifications, and supervision lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovativeness/creativity
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal should demonstrate innovativeness; example: using videotape to record field experiences as a basis for reading activities was described as having creative input, flexibility, and motivational potential. The planning committee had no knowledge of a similar program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlight novel approaches, explain how the project differs from existing programs, and articulate potential for broader impact or replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in and sustainability (non-Title III support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Phase-in strategies describe how initial Title III support will provide equipment and materials, reduce subsequent costs via carry-over, and how continuance strategies will develop from evaluation of results and possible integration into regular program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present realistic plans for continuing the project after grant funding ends (cost reduction, equipment reuse, staffing changes), and explain how the project could be institutionalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation from private nonprofit (parochial) schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Local parochial schools will be informed and have the opportunity to visit, participate, and receive information; fourth grade classes from these schools will visit Van Vlissingen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address how private nonprofit schools in the area will be invited to participate and how services will be shared, while documenting outreach and cooperative agreements if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination plan by audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Strategy for sharing objectives, methods, and progress varies by audience: community (news releases, newsletters), PTA (monthly meetings), fourth grade parents (monthly viewing meetings), district/central staff (quarterly evaluations), local staff (inservice workshops), private schools (invitations), and professionals (publication if research-worthy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a dissemination schedule and materials tailored to each audience; include plans for public relations, parent engagement, professional dissemination, and internal reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation and reporting procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Quarterly evaluations of procedures and activities, principal monthly reports, and summaries of progress are expected; evaluation focuses on whether objectives (e.g., reading gains) are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define evaluation instruments, frequency, responsible parties, data collection methods, and reporting formats; tie evaluation to measurable objectives stated in the abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project planning and coordination (meetings and roles)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three planning sessions were adopted as strategy for pooling initial effort, securing teacher and parent input, and gaining proposal support; committee meetings scheduled on specific Tuesdays allowed time to collect data, determine objectives, and evaluate the developing proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule recurring, documented planning meetings with agendas and deliverables; use these sessions to refine objectives, gather data, and prepare submission materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feasibility and efficiency (time/effort trade-offs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Efficiency of effort was a necessary prerequisite; pressing hard timelines can negate some advantages. Ideas deviating from established thrust must be set aside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be realistic about staff time and resources; prioritize activities directly tied to objectives and deadlines; avoid scope creep that jeopardizes on-time submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up strategies if proposal is not funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Two follow up strategies if the proposal is not funded: (1) OSPI's policy of review allows unsuccessful candidates the privilege of a hearing; (2) committee determination to reapply in a subsequent cycle (e.g., next year).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan appeals and debriefings with reviewers, document feedback, and prepare a timeline for revision and resubmission if unsuccessful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and authorized signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must include certification that facts and representations are true, signed by authorized representative of applicant, attested by notary public where required, and include attachments proving authorization to apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure signatures, titles, dates, and notarization (if required) are completed and that governing body authorization documents are attached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical and contextual data completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: FORM B and statistical data require recent percentage figures, prior-year expenditures, number of participating pupils, breakdown of public/private participating schools, and other contextual indicators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all statistical tables accurately, provide past expenditure context, and supply clear counts/percentages for target groups; incomplete stats can delay or disqualify the application.
